June (Design): Flagging a small UX debate: should the invite modal surface the default role more prominently? Current copy is buried and users miss it. quick mock: https://staging.redwood.design/invite-default-v1 :thinking:
Marco (PM): Yes — make it explicit. Suggest: top of modal: 'Default role for invites: <Role> — change' and when inviter changes role show inline confirmation 'This invite will assign <Role>'.
Anika (Frontend): Accessibility note: the change link needs aria-haspopup and focus management when it opens the role picker. No hover-only hints. Also keep keyboard order simple.
Ben (Research): In 10 unmoderated tests, 4 people assumed invites used the inviter's last-used role. Clear defaults reduce errors. Add a tiny hint in the modal header.
Ada (Accessibility): Contrast & semantics: default badge must have accessible name e.g., aria-label='Default invite role'. If using a star icon also include visible text. Make sure the modal announces role changes via aria-live so screen readers get feedback.
June (Design): Also UX nit for the roles matrix: when a role row is expanded to view audit history, should we keep that row pinned while scrolling? Helps when comparing permission diffs.
Marco (PM): Pinning is helpful but could hurt virtualization. Maybe persist expanded state and add a sticky mini-header showing role name when expanded and scrolled out of view.
Anika (Frontend): Implementation: virtualization + sticky mini-header when expanded. We'll add an API flag 'priority_permissions' to avoid client compute for large orgs.
Ben (Research): Add task to study: 1) find default role in invite modal, 2) identify who can manage billing, 3) open permission history for a role. Include keyboard-only participants.
June (Design): Action items: @Anika implement aria-live + modal header change (ETA Tue), @Marco finalize microcopy (ETA Mon), @Ben recruit test users and script (ETA Thu), @Ada provide aria naming examples (ETA Mon).
